requirement_text.REQ-157: Capability model and capability check at every gated host-function call site (LUA-05, LUA-06). Ports R-Co/src/lua/capabilities.zig (string-grant set with has/add) and R-Co/src/lua/host_api/mod.zig's registerAll capability matrix. Closed set of 8 platform.* functions: call_service->service:call:<svc_id>, read_variable->variable:read, write_variable->variable:write, log->audit:log, emit_event->event:emit, get_instance_state->instance:read, now->NONE (ungated by design), fail->NONE (ungated by design). Build: (1) capability-set representation + check function with structured denial details (function, capability required, capabilities granted); (2) single registration point enforcing the closed set (test that adding a 9th function without a matrix row fails); (3) denial raises a Lua error AND is reportable to host; (4) call_service grant is parameterised by service id, not blanket. NOT IN SCOPE: host functions' own bodies (REQ-159/160) beyond stubs needed to test the gate; platform.now already shipped (REQ-152). SECURITY-REVIEWER hard gate -- this is the authorization boundary for tenant-supplied scripts. Queue task 309, GH#609. See docs/requirements.yaml REQ-157 for full description and acceptance_criteria.

result.notes:
Reconciled test/specs/REQ-157.md against the actual shipped test suite (it was written before implementation existed, per Step 1 convention) -- updated §3/§4 to describe the real assertions and to record the gap found and closed.

AC-to-test mapping (8 ACs, docs/requirements.yaml REQ-157, verbatim):
1. 'exactly the eight functions ... enumerated from inside a script' -> platform_test.exs describe 'REQ-157: closed-set enumeration (AC1)', test 'a script enumerates exactly the 8 platform.* names via pairs(platform)' + source-level single-fold guard test.
2. 'for EACH of the six gated functions a capability-denial test' -> platform_test.exs describe 'REQ-157: per-function capability-denial tests, empty grant set (AC2)', 6 cases (read_variable/write_variable/log/emit_event/get_instance_state/call_service).
3. 'structured details include function, capability required, capabilities granted' -> now asserted on ALL SIX AC2 cases (was previously only bare assert_raise; see gap below), plus the dedicated 'REQ-157: structured denial fields (AC3)' case.
4. 'call_service("X") without service:call:X grant produces structured error' -> describe 'REQ-157: call_service denial without any grant (AC4)'.
5. 'service:call:alpha grant does NOT authorise call_service("beta")' -> describe 'REQ-157: call_service grant is parameterised, not blanket (AC5)', 2 cases.
6. 'now and fail callable with an EMPTY capability set' -> describe 'REQ-157: now and fail are callable with an empty capability set (AC6)', 2 cases.
7. 'moduledoc reproduces the capability matrix + now/fail rationale' -> describe 'REQ-157: moduledoc content (AC7)', 3 cases, reading Code.fetch_docs/1 on Platform's real moduledoc.
8. 'mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass' -> verified directly below, not asserted inside a test (matches design §9's own convention, TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 responsibility to re-confirm).

Coverage gap found and closed: the six AC2 per-function denial tests, as shipped by ELIXIR-DEV, used bare `assert_raise Lua.RuntimeException` with no field assertions. Every one of the six gated stubs (`run_stub(:not_yet_implemented, ...)`) raises Lua.RuntimeException unconditionally regardless of whether `Capabilities.check!/3` ran -- so a bug that silently skipped the capability check for one row would be indistinguishable from a genuine denial under a bare assert_raise. Confirmed by mutation-testing the shipped lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex directly: short-circuited `Capabilities.check!/3` for `write_variable` (`if row.name != :write_variable do Capabilities.check!(...) end`), ran `mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/platform_test.exs` -> 'Result: 27 passed' (mutant undetected). Reverted, then added capability_required/capabilities_granted/function field assertions to all six AC2 cases. Re-applied the identical mutant -> 'Result: 26/27 passed', exactly the write_variable case failing (`capability_required` observed nil instead of 'variable:write'). Reverted the mutant again (diff against pre-mutation backup confirmed byte-identical) -> full suite green again at 39 passed.

Wall-clock/randomness: read platform_test.exs's FixedTimeSource module and the 'the time source is injectable' describe block directly -- Application.put_env(:letflow, :lua_platform_time_source, FixedTimeSource) swaps in a fixed ~U[2026-01-01 00:00:00.000000Z] literal in setup, reverted via on_exit; no DateTime.utc_now/0, no sleep, no :rand anywhere in either test file.

Isolation: capabilities_test.exs is `async: true`, pure functions on locally-constructed MapSets, no shared state. platform_test.exs is `async: false` (documented reason: shared application-env mutation), every test that calls Application.put_env reverts it in on_exit; no test depends on another test's side effects; each denial test builds its own lua/grant fixture via `setup` or inline `Platform.install(Sandbox.new(), ...)`.
